tasks.short: Compile the exam from the item bank, check it with a second examiner, publish it in the testing environment, administer it, grade closed and open questions, and decide final scores with item analysis.

steps.what: Health specialties teacher compiles examinations from earlier questions and new ones
Health specialties teacher checks the final exam with a second examiner: questions match the test matrix, the answer key is right and the wording is clear
Health specialties teacher releases the checked exam: sending the file to the printing office today, by one release in the testing environment after the change
Health specialties teacher administers the examination
Health specialties teacher grades closed questions with an answer key
Health specialties teacher grades open answers against the rubric

loop.input: Students' answers to one open question and the rubric.
loop.output: Groups of similar answers with a proposed rubric score per group.
loop.check: Similar answers are grouped but no score is proposed; the examiner reads every answer and sets every score; a second examiner double-marks a sample, and agreement is computed.
loop.stop: If agreement on the sample falls below the agreed level, grouping is switched off for that question and answers are marked one by one.
loop.why_not_simpler: Open answers say the same thing in different words; a keyword rule cannot group them.

steps.what: Health specialties teacher runs the item analysis on closed and open scores
Health specialties teacher decides final scores after item analysis

tasks.design: Questions sit in an item bank in the digital testing environment ({LMS}) tagged by learning outcome, so an exam is compiled against the test matrix instead of from old files. Once checked with a second examiner, the teacher releases the exam in the testing environment. Closed questions are marked by the answer key. For open answers a bounded step groups similar answers and proposes no score; the examiner reads every answer and sets every score, and a double-marked sample guards agreement. Item analysis is computed by code. Final scores stay with the examiner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exams were built from old files, printed and marked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital testing environments hold item banks and group similar open answers.
tasks.still_hard: Clinical skills exams need observation, not software.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a half-right answer shows safe clinical reasoning.
tasks.altitude: The examiner sets scores on grouped answers instead of marking one paper at a time.

reach.learn: Whether item analysis improves weak questions.

evidence.claim: Gradescope groups similar answers so each group is graded once.
At Penn State Harrisburg, a physics professor estimated answer grouping cut grading time by over half on 170 exams; vendor case.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk under Annex III point 3; here the examiner sets every score.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set results.

assumptions: Boundary: from the test matrix to final scores; registering grades and fraud cases are outside.
Input contract: item bank kept by the course team; fallback is paper exams and hand marking.
The examiner sets every score.
A DPIA comes before grouping student answers.
Pricing of s7: item statistics are computed by the testing environment instead of by copying scores into a spreadsheet; the teacher only opens the report, about 15% of the step.
s1 keeps 60 because new questions are still written by hand; s3 keeps 20 for the release; s6 keeps 70 because grouping saves repeated judgement but every answer is read and scored by the examiner.
research_questions: What is the agreement between grouped and one-by-one marking?

already_counted.description: Health specialties teacher reviews grouped answers.

incremental.description: Health specialties teacher tags new items in the item bank.

approvals.approved_version: The exam with questions, answer key and settings exactly as checked with the second examiner in s2, released once in the testing environment for this sitting; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the item bank holds few items yet, so s1 keeps 85, and grouping helps little on varied answers, so s6 keeps 90 (26.1); high: bank and grouping as assumed (37.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

Students sign the practical attendance list
Health specialties teacher combines grades in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Students check in to practicals by scanning a code in the learning environment ({LMS}). Its gradebook computes weighted grades by the course rules, and students see their grade breakdown in the portal. Once the examiner has checked final grades, the teacher passes them to student administration ({OTHER}) in one transfer without retyping. Students log the hours actually worked in their e-portfolio and placement supervisors confirm them, instead of paper logs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attendance lists, grade spreadsheets and grades typed into two systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning environments compute weighted grades and pass them to student administration.
tasks.still_hard: Exceptions such as exemptions and resits need the examiner.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining to a student why a clinical rotation must be redone.
tasks.altitude: The teacher checks grades and handles exceptions instead of computing and typing.

reach.learn: Whether clinical hour records are complete.

evidence.claim: At Radboud, grades entered in Brightspace must also be published in OSIRIS, a double entry.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set results.

assumptions: Boundary: from the practical list to required records kept; examination board decisions are outside.
Input contract: class lists from student administration; grading rules set by the examiner; fallback is paper and spreadsheets.

Students scan a code in about the time signing took (s2); their hours log (s5b) and the supervisor's confirmation (s5c) replace paper logs and signatures. s1 keeps 20 for exceptions; s5 keeps 10 for the transfer; s6 keeps 50 for records still kept by hand.
Checking final grades stays with the examiner.

Students look up their grade breakdown in the portal.

tasks.design: A shared case bank in the document space ({DOCS}) holds anonymised clinical cases with questions per learning outcome, so teachers adapt cases instead of writing each one. The teacher writes the summary in a template after class, checks it and posts it once to the course page ({LMS}). Leading the discussion stays with the teacher.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared case banks are easy to keep in a document space.
tasks.still_hard: A good discussion depends on the group, not the case.
tasks.human_edge: Drawing out the student who saw a similar patient on placement.
tasks.altitude: Teachers adapt shared cases; leading the discussion stays.

evidence.claim: Shared case banks in document spaces let teachers reuse and adapt cases.

assumptions: Boundary: from the lesson plan to the summary posted; exams are outside.
Input contract: cases anonymised and added by the teaching team; fallback is writing own cases.
Moderating discussions does not change.
Students read the summary as they would class notes; no added student time.
s1 keeps 70 for adapting cases; s3 keeps 85 because the template gives only the layout; s4 keeps 20 for posting.

tasks.short: Review course evaluations and results, discuss revisions with the curriculum committee, revise course content and the manual, update clinical cases and materials, check the course with the coordinator, and publish it.

steps.what: Health specialties teacher evaluates the course from student evaluations and results
Health specialties teacher discusses curricula revisions with the curriculum committee
Health specialties teacher revises course content and the course manual

loop.input: The agreed revisions, the catalogue's learning outcomes and the current manual.
loop.output: Draft revised sections of the course manual.
loop.check: Code checks every learning outcome is covered by at least one week and one assessment; the teacher checks that each drafted section says what the committee agreed, and edits and approves the text.
loop.stop: Stops when coverage passes and the teacher approves, or after two failed redrafts the teacher writes the section.
loop.why_not_simpler: Manual sections explain the course in prose; a coverage table alone does not.

steps.what: Health specialties teacher updates clinical cases and course materials
Health specialties teacher checks the revised course with the programme coordinator: manual, cases and materials match the agreed revisions
Health specialties teacher publishes the checked course materials in the learning environment

tasks.design: A course dashboard ({BI}) joins student evaluation scores, pass rates and item analysis. A bounded step drafts revised manual sections from the agreed changes; code checks every learning outcome is covered, and the teacher edits. Clinical cases are updated in the shared case bank. Once the coordinator has agreed, the teacher publishes the course in the learning environment ({LMS}). Deciding revisions with the committee stays with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evaluation data sat in separate files and manuals were reworked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Dashboards join course data; language models draft text from agreed changes.
tasks.still_hard: Clinical guidelines change and course content must follow.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing which new guideline students must learn now.
tasks.altitude: The teacher decides revisions and edits drafts instead of reworking materials by hand.

evidence.claim: EduGenAI is a chat platform for Dutch education in pilot at Utrecht University, which forbids automated grading on it.
Revising course manuals is not an Annex III use; AI that evaluates learning outcomes is.

assumptions: Boundary: from course results to the course published; programme-level changes are outside.
Input contract: evaluations and results from the institution's systems; learning outcomes from the catalogue; fallback is reworking by hand.
Committee discussions do not change.
No student names or patient data go into the drafting step.
s1 keeps 40 for reading the dashboard; s3 keeps 70 because drafts give standard parts and the teacher writes the rest; s4 keeps 70; s6 keeps 20 for publishing.
research_questions: Do pass rates change after revisions?
